articleBlocks: At first, Crust and Mantle pointed in a few different directions, so the board still felt wider than one exact category. One tempting read was "a broader umbrella topic". Crust, Mantle can point toward several nearby themes before one clue makes the exact category level visible. Core (mostly iron and nickel) is the clue that narrows the board into one category with clearer boundaries. Another nearby read was "a one-clue surface theme". Early clues often tempt you to overfit the board around one obvious surface similarity. The final answer works because it keeps every clue at the same level of specificity, not because one clue happens to fit first.
Once I read the set through a category board focused on parts, examples like "Category example: Crust" and "Category example: Mantle" stopped feeling loose and started landing cleanly.

Core (mostly iron and nickel), Tectonic plates, Magnetic poles (North+South) keep the clues at the same category level, which is what makes the board feel like one exact set instead of a broad umbrella theme.

The answer was "Parts of the Earth". More precisely, the board resolves as one concrete category with members that stay at the same level of specificity as Parts of the Earth, which is why "Parts of the Earth" fits better than "a broader umbrella topic" or "a one-clue surface theme" once the full set is checked.
solutionNarrative: I started by testing Crust and Mantle, but that only gave me a loose direction. I initially drifted toward a broader umbrella topic, because the first clues could still fit several nearby ideas. I held the guess until one clue gave me a more specific way to read the list.

The turn came when I let "Core (mostly iron and nickel)" lead the solve. After that, Tectonic plates and Magnetic poles (North+South) became the real confirmation check, because they had to fit the same idea without changing the rule or stretching the answer.

For the final pass, I checked Crust, Mantle, Core (mostly iron and nickel), Tectonic plates, Magnetic poles (North+South) one by one. The answer worked only if the whole list could stay inside one tight reading, not because one early clue happened to match a broad topic.
The answer was "Parts of the Earth".
